title: "Building an R bioinformatics Package with a Rust Backend"
description: "A library for fast read-level analysis of long-read FASTQ files"
date: 2025-09-30
categories: [R, Rust, bioinformatics, side project]
---

Analyzing long-read FASTQ data in R can be challenging. The **ShortRead** R library exists, but it was designed for short reads and struggles with the longer lengths typical of long-read sequencing. Existing Python-based tools provide only high-level summaries, lacking read-level detail.

To address this, I developed an R library that leverages **Rust** to efficiently process FASTQ files and extract subsets of reads based on GC content, average quality score, and read length. Installation details can be found [here](https://github.com/sparthib/longReads).

### Rust + R: Speeding up bioinformatics

R excels at statistics and visualization, but parsing large long-read FASTQ files can be slow. Rust brings:

-   Memory safety without garbage collection overhead

-   High performance for CPU-intensive tasks

-   Seamless interoperability with R via **extendr**

By combining Rust with R, I kept compute-heavy operations in Rust while maintaining the familiar R interface for analysis and visualization.

## Introducing `longReads`

`longReads` provides a fast **read-level summary** of FASTQ files. The main function, `analyze_fastq_r`, outputs a list with these columns:

| Column        | Description                      |
|---------------|----------------------------------|
| `read_id`     | Identifier of the read           |
| `length`      | Length of the read in base pairs |
| `avg_quality` | Average Phred quality score      |
| `gc_content`  | GC content percentage            |

It uses [`bio::io::fastq`](https://docs.rs/bio/latest/bio/io/fastq/) for parsing in Rust and exposes the results to R.

You can try it out by following the instructions [here](https://github.com/sparthib/longReads).\
